einzeiler: Final midterms preview with a look at the New York Times polls and Haley Stevens'…
kurzfassung: The hosts review the final batch of New York Times polls showing a strong upward trajectory for Democrats across Senate and gubernatorial races. They discuss the unexpected endorsement drama surrounding Haley Stevens in Michigan and investigate ballot manipulation allegations in Alaska. Finally, they share their final predictions and analyze how broader economic and political shifts are shaping the electorate.
stichpunkte: The final New York Times poll of the cycle shows Democrats leading or tied in every key Senate and gubernatorial race.
Polling aggregator Flipper gives Democrats an 80 percent chance of taking the Senate and a 96 percent chance of winning the House.
Early voting data indicates Democratic voters are outpacing 2024 turnout levels across multiple battleground states.
Haley Stevens endorses Republican Mike Rogers in Michigan, sparking intense personal and intra-party fallout.
An investigation reveals operatives linked to Mary Peltola's campaign were behind a decoy candidate scheme in Alaska.
Federal judges dismiss a Department of Justice lawsuit aimed at blocking election results in Alaska.
The hosts analyze the intersection of 2006-style populist backlashes and 2018 suburban voting trends in this cycle.

clips.hook: An election cycle unlike any recent stress test
clips.text: Reflecting on how unique this election feels compared to the stressful atmosphere of previous cycles, the hosts note that covering it has been genuinely exciting.

clips.hook: Current odds for the Senate and House majorities
clips.text: The statistical model gives Democrats an 80 percent probability of capturing the Senate and a 96 percent chance of winning the House.

clips.hook: The limited political weight of a primary bloc
clips.text: Analyzing a controversial primary endorsement, it is pointed out that the endorser represents only a tiny fraction of primary voters and lacks broader influence.
Using confusing ballot maneuvers directly undermines the core message that a political party stands for democratic norms and fair voting practices.
Voters supported specific policies when they were initially proposed, but the resulting negative consequences ultimately triggered a powerful public backlash.

beschreibung:
In this bonus episode, Clare, Nate, and Galen take a last look at FLIPR’s midterm forecast and the latest New York Times/Siena University polls—both of which show Democrats with a lot of momentum heading into Election Day. They also unpack Haley Stevens’ eleventh-hour endorsement of Abdul El-Sayed’s opponent, Mike Rogers, and ballot-stacking in Alaska before sharing their final midterm predictions.
